Cryptographic Operations Team, we are recording the authoritative fifteen-step ceremony protocol for initializing the production hardware security module cluster.

Before starting key generation, verify that the dual-camera video recording systems have synchronized their timestamps against Stratum 1 GPS time servers. The security officer must inspect the Faraday cage enclosure to confirm that radio-frequency shielding attenuates wireless signals by at least 80 decibels. In addition, run hardware diagnostics using `tools/hsm_diag.py` to verify that FIPS 140-2 Level 3 tamper switches are fully operational.

The first key custodian, Alice; second key custodian, Bob; and third key custodian, Charlie, must present government-issued photo identification to the compliance auditor. The biometric iris scanner at the vault entrance must record access events with cryptographic timestamp receipts. The clean-room environment must be continuously purged with positive-pressure HEPA filtration systems to prevent airborne particulate contamination.

Under no circumstances should any participant connect unapproved external USB devices or recording apparatus to the ceremony consoles.

Step one: Verify physical tamper-evident seals on the HSM chassis and log serial numbers in the compliance ledger.

Step two: Connect dual redundant power feeds to isolated uninterruptible power supplies in cage four.

Step three: Establish an out-of-band serial console connection using a 9,600 baud rate, with hardware flow control enabled.

Step four: Power on the master HSM appliance and verify that secure boot cryptographic signatures validate successfully.

Step five: Initialize the master security domain using three of five M-of-N administrative smart cards.

Step six: Generate the root master key pair using elliptic curve secp256k1 inside the secure cryptographic boundary.

Step seven: Export the public certificate signing request while ensuring private key material never leaves volatile tamper-protected memory.

Step eight: Transmit the certificate signing request to the offline root certificate authority via air-gapped optical media.

Step nine: Import the signed X.509 root identity certificate into the HSM key store.

Step ten: Configure automated cryptographic partition backup replication to the secondary standby HSM over a dedicated point-to-point IPsec tunnel.

Step eleven: Set partition access control policies enforcing role-based separation between crypto officers and crypto users.

Step twelve: Execute synthetic signature benchmark transactions, verifying the HSM processes at least 2,000 RSA-4096 signatures per second.

Step thirteen: Enable audit logging to a remote syslog server with cryptographic signature chaining enabled.

Step fourteen: Deposit administrative smart cards and physical PIN codes into dual-custody safe deposit boxes.

Step fifteen: Obtain formal ceremony completion signatures from the lead security auditor and chief risk officer before declaring the cluster operational.

Under no circumstances should any single security officer possess more than two administrative smart cards during the initialization ceremony.

The security operations director confirmed that if any physical chassis seal shows signs of tampering, the ceremony must be aborted immediately. All video surveillance recordings of the ceremony area must be archived for seven years in compliance with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards.

In addition, inspect `smartcard_reader.py` in the ceremony scripts folder to verify PIN pad input sanitization routines. The ceremony administrator must confirm that PKCS #11 driver libraries in `/usr/lib/libpkcs11.so` load without dynamic linker warnings.

When generating the certificate revocation list, verify that CRL distribution point URLs point to `https://cki.enterprise.com/crl/root.crl`. The OCSP responder signing certificate must enforce non-repudiation and digital signature key usage, with a validity lifespan of three years.

Verify that the RSA private key exponent is set to 65,537 to protect against low-exponent cryptographic attacks. In addition, audit the offline entropy pool using `dd if=/dev/hwrng` to collect two megabytes of random bits and confirm zero correlation spikes across bit patterns.

The legal counsel witness confirmed that all digital signatures must be witnessed by two notary publics present in the secure room throughout the session. Moreover, confirm that the root certificate authority subject distinguished name specifies common name Enterprise Root CA, organizational unit Security Engineering, organization Global Enterprise Corporation, and country code US.

After the ceremony concludes, all disposable paper notes, wiping cloths, and packaging materials must be shredded in a cross-cut shredder meeting DIN 66399 Level 6 security standards. All smart cards must be initialized using AES-256-bit transport encryption keys before storing master seed material. The witness log must record the precise manufacturer batch number and firmware hash for every smart card used during the ceremony.

In addition, verify that electromagnetic emanations from the cryptographic workstation comply with TEMPEST Level A shielding requirements. Furthermore, ensure that temperature sensors inside the HSM cage alert when ambient temperature exceeds 22 degrees Celsius.

The disaster recovery runbook in `docs/security/hsm_recovery.md` must be updated with the new partition identifier numbers. The facilities team must also certify that backup diesel generators have 60 hours of fuel on site. In addition, verify that emergency exit doors are monitored with magnetic contact sensors throughout the session. Finally, verify that all emergency power cutoff switches in the cryptographic enclosure are tested and certified by Facilities Engineering.
